claim: The KOSPI [South Korea's stock index] rose almost 200% in the 12 months before [late June 2026]
quote: it's gone up almost 200% in the last 12 months
evidence: KOSPI closed 2025 at 4,214.17 (+76% YoY) and closed near 3,021.84 in June 2025; it hit an all-time closing high of 9,385.59 on 19 Jun 2026. (9,385.59-3,021.84)/3,021.84 ≈ +211% trailing 12mo — at or above the claimed 'almost 200%,' not an exaggeration.

claim: The S&P 500 rose 24% over the same trailing 12 months, by comparison
quote: the US's S&P 500, which only made 24%
evidence: S&P 500 calendar-2025 total return was ~17-18%; close-to-close Jul 2025→Jul 2026 (6,339.39→7,489.72) is +18.1%. Both real measures run 6-8 points below the claimed 24% (a ~35% relative overstatement), which inflates the KOSPI-vs-US comparison.

claim: The top 10 companies in the S&P 500 represent 36% of the index
quote: the top 10 companies represent 36% of this index
evidence: JPMorgan AM and Pensions & Investments both put 2026 top-10 S&P 500 weight at 37-41%. The claimed 36% is close and, if anything, conservative.

claim: [Samsung] was up over 500% at one point in 2026
quote: Samsung, was up over 500%
evidence: Reporting on Samsung's 2026 rally puts its peak gain at roughly 5.7x (≈+470%) for the year — close to but short of the claimed 'over 500%'; within range given the stock kept moving after the cited reports.

claim: [SK Hynix] was up over 1,000% at one point in 2026
quote: SK Hynix was up over 1,000%
evidence: Reported SK Hynix 2026 gains cluster at +250% (May), +167% (Jul) and +430% (1-year, later print) — real and dramatic, but 2-4x short of the claimed 'over 1,000%.' No source found supporting a 4-digit gain at any point.

claim: Samsung and SK Hynix together represent over 56% of the whole KOSPI [South Korean stock market]
quote: represent over 56% of their whole stock market
evidence: 50.44% combined as of 27 May 2026; by ~22 Jun 2026 Samsung (~2,246tn KRW incl. preferred) + SK Hynix (~2,085tn KRW) ≈ 4,331tn KRW against a total KOSPI market cap of ~7,000tn KRW ≈ 62%. 'Over 56%' sits inside that range, not inflated.

claim: South Korea has roughly 14 million retail investors, about one in four of its 51 million population
quote: roughly 14 million retail investors
evidence: Korea Securities Depository data put individual investors at ~14 million, about a quarter of Korea's ~51.7 million population; a later count reached 14.56 million by end-2025. Matches the claim closely.

claim: The KOSPI dropped 25% in 21 days [ending around the video's 20 Jul 2026 publish date]
quote: in just 21 days, everything started to collapse. The KOSPI dropped 25%
evidence: KOSPI hit its all-time closing high of 9,385.59 on 19 Jun 2026 and had fallen 25% from that peak by 16 Jul 2026 (28 days) — very close to the claimed window if measured to the video's 'three weeks ago' reference point around 29 Jun.

claim: 1.2 million Korean brokerage accounts, or about one in every 30 people in the country, got hit with margin call thresholds during the crash
quote: 1.2 million accounts, which works out to be one in every 30 people in the country, got hit with
evidence: By 13 Jul 2026, over 1.2 million leveraged retail accounts had triggered margin calls, reported elsewhere as 'roughly 1 in every 30 working-age adults' — the video says '1 in 30 people' rather than 'working-age adults,' a minor, non-material simplification of the same ratio.

claim: Over 3 trillion won in Korean stock investments were forcibly liquidated during the crash
quote: over 3 trillion won in investments were liquidated
evidence: Cumulative forced liquidations reached 2.3 trillion won from May through 14 Jul 2026 — real and large, but about 23% short of the claimed 'over 3 trillion.' Continued selling through the video's 20 Jul publish date plausibly pushed the total higher, but I could not find a figure at or above 3tn won directly. Best sources reachable were tier 4, which also caps this below confirmed.

claim: 320,000 Korean brokerage accounts were wiped out, some overnight
quote: 320,000 accounts were just wiped out
evidence: Multiple reports put forced liquidations at 360,000 accounts (not 320,000) alongside the same 1.2 million margin-call figure — the claimed count is about 11% below what's reported, same order of magnitude, tier-4 sourcing only.

claim: The president of South Korea held an emergency intervention for the stock market in 2026
quote: the president of South Korea held an emergency intervention for their stock market
evidence: President Lee convened an emergency meeting in early August 2026 on real estate and stock-market policy amid the crash, and separately touted a 100tn won ($68bn) stabilization program earlier in the year — matches the claim's substance.

claim: [An investor profiled in a documentary about the Korean stock mania] had a portfolio worth over $650,000 and was up 150%, mostly in leveraged ETFs
quote: Her portfolio was worth over $650,000, and she was up 150%
evidence: A single unnamed individual's private portfolio and returns, sourced only to an unnamed documentary — no outside party can check this by construction.

claim: At the peak, Koreans invested about 10 trillion won into leveraged funds betting on one company
quote: invested about 10 trillion won into leveraged funds betting on just one company
evidence: Single-stock leveraged ETFs launched with over 10tn won ($6.9bn) in first-day trading value, and combined AUM across the category peaked at 17.6tn won in late June 2026. 10tn won for the single largest name at some point in that run is plausible but not pinned to an exact date in what I found.

claim: Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta spent $376 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025 and are on track to spend $725 billion in 2026
quote: $376 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025… on track to spend 725 billion
evidence: The $725B 2026 figure matches reporting almost exactly. But the 2025 actual/guidance figures reported are higher: 'more than $380 billion' guidance (Oct 2025) and '~$410 billion' in later retrospective coverage — $376B sits below both, consistent with an earlier, lower guidance snapshot rather than the final 2025 number.

claim: In one trading session [in mid-to-late June 2026], the KOSPI dropped something like 4.6%
quote: the KOSPI dropped something like 4.6%
evidence: Named gap: searched for a ~4.6% single-session KOSPI drop in the window before Black Tuesday (23 Jun); the closest match found was the KOSPI opening 4.46% lower on 2 Jul — after Black Tuesday, not before, which doesn't fit the video's own stated sequence (4.6% session → a week later a 9%+ day → Black Tuesday). Per my memory of wire-headline pitfalls, an intraday or opening figure can also differ from the session close; I could not confirm which this refers to.

claim: Samsung and SK Hynix both went down more than 9% in one day, a week after that session
quote: both went down more than 9% in just one day
evidence: On 23 Jun 2026 (Black Tuesday), Samsung and SK Hynix both ended the session down more than 12% — worse than the claimed 9%, so directionally confirmed, though the reporting I found places this on the same day as Black Tuesday rather than a week before it (see claim 16).

claim: On Black Tuesday [23 Jun 2026], the KOSPI went down more than 10% in a day
quote: the KOSPI went down more than 10% in just a day
evidence: KOSPI fell 9.99% on 23 Jun 2026 ('Black Tuesday'), the fifth-largest single-day percentage decline and largest points-drop in its history — a hair under the claimed 'more than 10%,' close enough to be the same event but technically not the wording used.

claim: A 10% one-day drop in the US stock market would be the third-worst day in American history, behind only 1987 and the Great Depression
quote: that would be the third worst day in American history, only behind 1987 and the Great Depression
evidence: Ranked S&P 500 one-day drops: -20.47% (19 Oct 1987), -12.34% (28 Oct 1929), -11.98% (16 Mar 2020, COVID), -10.16% (29 Oct 1929), -9.92% (6 Nov 1929). A -10.0% day would rank roughly 4th-6th, not 3rd, and the March 2020 COVID crash — not 1987 or the Depression — is the one that would actually sit ahead of it. The claim omits 2020 and understates how many worse days the Depression alone had.

claim: Korean margin-account forced-liquidation rates rose from about 2% under normal conditions to over 10% during the crash — about five times normal
quote: about 2% of Korean margin accounts get force liquidated… went higher than 10%, which is about five times the normal rate
evidence: For the week of 10 Jul 2026, the forced-liquidation rate surged above 10%, versus an average of 2.1% over the prior six months — 10/2.1 ≈ 4.8x, matching 'about five times' almost exactly.

claim: Over the next two days [after Black Tuesday], more than $600 billion got erased from Asian markets, and Japan went down more than 4%
quote: more than 600 billion dollars got erased from Asian markets… Japan went down more than 4%
evidence: One reported episode: ~$650bn wiped off Asian stocks in a selloff, with Japan's Nikkei down 3.1% and KOSPI down 5.5% on that occasion — the aggregate figure matches ('more than 600bn'), but the specific Japan decline found (3.1%) falls short of the claimed 'more than 4%.'

claim: At one point, a national holiday market closure was the only thing that stopped the KOSPI from falling further
quote: the market was literally closed for a national holiday
evidence: Named gap: searched Korea's June-July 2026 crash timeline for a specific market-holiday closure that halted a slide; found detailed circuit-breaker and trading-halt coverage but no report naming a national holiday as what stopped a particular leg down.

claim: South Korea's president had spent a year before the crash encouraging people to get into the stock market
quote: spent a year encouraging people to get into the stock market
evidence: Reporting describes authorities trying to attract more retail capital into stocks earlier in 2026, including offering high-risk products to retail investors, and President Lee's own market-friendly rhetoric — consistent with, though not a direct one-source confirmation of, 'spent a year encouraging.'

claim: As of June 2026, US margin debt hit roughly 4.5% of GDP, the highest level ever recorded — higher than the dot-com bubble, 2007, and the 2021 meme-stock bubble
quote: roughly 4 and 1/2% of GDP. That is the highest level ever recorded in American history
evidence: FINRA margin debt hit a record $1.53tn in June 2026; margin debt/GDP is independently reported at ~4.5%, a new record surpassing the peaks before the 2000 dot-com crash, 2008 financial crisis, and 2021 meme-stock top — matches the claim closely.

claim: Every time US margin debt has gone to an extreme [1968, 1972, 1987, 2000, 2007, 2018, 2021], a crash has followed almost right after, every single time
quote: every time US margin debt went to an extreme, a crash happened almost right after, every single time
evidence: The general pattern is well documented: margin debt peaked in March 2000 (2.66% of GDP) right before the dot-com crash, and again in July 2007 before the financial crisis; rapid margin-debt contraction also coincided with 1929, 1987 and 2020. I could not individually verify the 1968, 1972, 2018 and 2021 instances the video lists, so the absolute framing ('every single time') is stronger than what I confirmed, though the core mechanism checks out.

claim: [Jim Chanos] said hyperscaler incremental operating margin on AI spending has gone from 40% a year and a half ago to about 20% today, and is moving toward 10%
quote: gone from as a group 40% a year and a half ago to about 20% today… moving toward 10%
evidence: Independent conference reporting attributes Chanos with the same 40%→20%→toward-10% incremental-margin figures, matching the clip almost verbatim. Best independently reachable write-up is tier 4, which caps this below confirmed even though the video's own clip is direct audio of the remark.

claim: [OpenAI and Anthropic] still lose tens of billions of dollars a year but make up 70 to 80% of all AI compute demand
quote: they still lose tens of billions of dollars a year… they make up 70 to 80% of all the AI compute demand
evidence: Independent reporting puts OpenAI+Anthropic at 75-85% of current/future AI compute spend (and ~75% of the big three hyperscalers' AI data-center capacity) — brackets the claimed 70-80% well. Losses: OpenAI ~$14bn (2026 guidance, cash burn estimated up to $27bn) plus Anthropic ~$2bn ('$16bn' combined on the low estimate, higher under cash-burn estimates) — 'tens of billions' is defensible on the higher-end reading but not the conservative one.

claim: In 2026, IPOs have come to market at over 12% of GDP in post-IPO market cap, versus a previous record of 5% at the dot-com peak
quote: IPOs have come to market at over 12% of GDP in post-IPO market cap… the previous record was the peak of the dot-com bubble at just 5%
evidence: Named gap: searched IPO proceeds vs GDP, dot-com era issuance ratios, and market-cap-to-GDP framing across three angles. Found strong data on aggregate US market cap/GDP (a record 235-238%, exceeding the dot-com peak) and on absolute 2026 IPO dollar volume (~$200bn, above combined 1999-2000), but never located a source using the specific 'post-IPO market cap as % of GDP' metric to check the stated 12% vs 5% figures directly.

claim: In 2000, Coca-Cola cut its order of routers from Cisco from 10,000 to 2,000, and Cisco's earnings collapsed as a result
quote: Coca-Cola needed 10,000 routers from Cisco. By 2001, they needed only 2,000
evidence: Fabrication-tell candidate: search is clearly working — it surfaces extensive, specific coverage of Cisco's real 2001 bullwhip-effect inventory crisis and $2.25bn write-down, including other named-customer case studies — but three separate searches (direct, bullwhip-effect, case-study angles) found no trace of a Coca-Cola order cut from 10,000 to 2,000 routers specifically. A named, checkable specific with no footprint despite an otherwise-productive search.

claim: The NASDAQ went down 78% in the dot-com bust that followed
quote: the NASDAQ went down 78%
evidence: NASDAQ Composite peaked 10 Mar 2000 at 5,132.52 and bottomed 10 Oct 2002 at 1,108.49-1,114, a decline of 77.9-78% — matches the claim exactly. (The mechanism attributed — the Coca-Cola/Cisco anecdote — is separately unverified; see claim 29.)

claim: [Jim Chanos] predicts the AI-spending reckoning could arrive sometime in late 2026 or 2027
quote: sometime in late 2026 or 2027
evidence: A real, independently-reported Chanos view, consistent with his separately-verified incremental-margin thesis (claim 26). It is honestly hedged with a wide window ('late 2026 or 2027') rather than a specific date, and the video itself flags the follow-on Shrek-movie bit as a joke rather than evidence.

claim: [DeleteMe] was named the number one data removal service by [Wirecutter]
quote: They were just named the number one data removal service by Wirecutter
evidence: NYT Wirecutter named DeleteMe the 'best data removal service' in its 2025 review — matches the claim, though it is a sponsor-read claim about the sponsor (tier-4 self-interest) independently corroborated by the cited outlet.

claim: [The speaker's] own DeleteMe account found and removed over 68 instances of his info being sold, saving an estimated 14.5 hours
quote: removed over 68 instances of someone selling my info… an estimated 14 and a half hours of trying to get this info removed
evidence: A personal account of one user's own data-removal activity inside a paid sponsorship read — private to the speaker and the vendor, unverifiable by construction.

claim: The vice president of the company that owned the Titanic said 'We have absolute confidence in the Titanic. We believe the boat is unsinkable' in April 1912, after it had already sunk
quote: We have absolute confidence in the Titanic. We believe the boat is unsinkable.
evidence: Real quote: Philip Franklin, vice-president of White Star Line, said this on the morning of 15 April 1912, hours after Titanic had already sunk — matches the claim's attribution, wording and timing.
